label: prop:q-beta-bar-even-kernel-invariant
title: $\mathfrak{Q}_\beta$ precision-ladder $\bar{}$-even discriminant — the kernel $R(q,\xi)$ produces a clean integer-$u$ ladder $\prod_k(1+c_k\,u^k)$ if and only if $R$ is even under $t \mapsto -t$ ($t = q-1$); $(1-u^2)$ at N=2 is the prototype
html:
Proposition. \mathfrak{Q}_\beta precision-ladder \bar{}-even discriminant — the kernel R(q,\xi) produces a clean integer-u ladder \prod_k(1+c_k\,u^k) if and only if R is even under t \mapsto -t (t = q-1); (1-u^2) at N=2 is the prototype

In the \mathfrak{Q}_\beta ladder

  R(u) := \prod_k(1 + c_k u^k), \qquad u = b(q) \cdot \hbar_q^2,

the ladder admits a clean integer-u Taylor representation if and only if R is bar-even (an even function of t := q - 1 about q = 1).

The substrate variable u has a double zero at q = 1. Under q \mapsto q^{-1}, t \mapsto -t + O(t^2). If R is even in t, the u-grading absorbs the coefficients, avoiding a \sqrt{u} branch. If R has odd-in-t content, the reversion picks up a \sqrt{u} branch, making the scalar extraction singular.

This is the formalize-first gate for the bar-even invariant. We state the candidate as a power series in t. We compute R(q^{-1}, \xi^{-1}) and subtract. A non-zero difference refutes the candidate structurally.
